# Breadcrumbs

Pass items in route order, each with a label and href. The final item is always marked as the current page; separators appear only between items. Each item accepts native link attributes and a class override. Decorative separators are included inside ancestor links. The default aria-label is translated; override it to distinguish multiple navigation landmarks.

## Usage

```ts
import { Breadcrumbs } from '$lib/io/breadcrumbs';
```

Pass `items` in hierarchy order, each with a `label` and `href`. The final item
receives `aria-current="page"`; separators are decorative. The navigation has a
translated accessible label, which can be overridden with `aria-label`.

The trail wraps when space is constrained.

## Selection

Breadcrumbs display the current page, allows for navigation to different levels of the hierarchy.

| Do                                                                                                                                                           | Don't                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **USE-1** Reflect the real page hierarchy, from the broadest level down to the current page, such as Namespaces › production › Workflows › order-processing. | **USE-2** Don't use breadcrumbs to show the user's browsing history. They describe where a page sits, not how the user got there. |
| **USE-3** Use the same names as the pages they link to, so each crumb matches the title users see when they arrive.                                          | **USE-4** Don't use breadcrumbs on top-level pages. A single crumb adds noise without helping users navigate.                     |
| **USE-5** Place breadcrumbs at the top of the page, above the page title.                                                                                    | **USE-6** Don't replace primary navigation with breadcrumbs. They are a secondary aid for moving up the hierarchy.                |
| **USE-7** Keep labels short. Use the object's name or ID rather than a full description.                                                                     | **USE-8** Don't add actions, menus, or icons to crumbs. Each crumb should be a plain link.                                        |

## Rules

Checked against every PR that uses this component.

### Accessibility

- **A11Y-1** If a page contains multiple distinct breadcrumb trails, callers MUST give each trail a distinct accessible label with `aria-label`. The shared translated default does not distinguish them.

## Notes

How the component behaves. Context for reviewers; not checked.

- **BEH-1** Items render as TextLinks inside an ordered list and a navigation landmark. The last item receives `aria-current="page"`; it remains a link.
- **BEH-2** Separators are decorative trailing icons inside ancestor links. The list wraps when space is constrained.
- **BEH-3** Item attributes are forwarded to [TextLink](../text-link/text-link.svelte). Wrapper attributes, including `data-testid`, reach the nav. No test ID is assigned internally.

## API Reference

| Name       | Description | Type                    | Default                      | Required |
| ---------- | ----------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------- |
| items      |             | `readonly Breadcrumb[]` | —                            | Yes      |
| aria-label |             | `string`                | `"Breadcrumbs" (translated)` | No       |
